### Makeover

![Three-panel unit chart titled "The typical balloon stayed the same size. Giants became more common." Each panel is a 10-by-10 grid in which every square stands for 1 in every 100 hot-air balloons recorded in US states, grouped by build period; burgundy squares mark giants, rated over 211,900 cubic feet, more than twice the typical balloon. Giants rose from 2 squares in 2000–2009 (2.2%, 26 of 1,198 recorded builds) to 9 in 2010–2019 (8.5%, 78 of 914) and a full top row of 10 in 2020–2026 (9.9%, 67 of 675), with most of the rise coming in the 2010s. The median rated envelope volume stayed at 90,000 cubic feet in every period. Outside the US, the giant share stayed near 5%. Data: The Hot Air Balloon Database, via Kaggle; 2026 is a partial year.](mm_2026_45.png){#fig-1}

### [**Steps to Create this Graphic**]{.mark}

#### [1. Load Packages & Setup]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: load
#| warning: false
#| message: false      
#| results: "hide"     

## 1. LOAD PACKAGES & SETUP ----
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
  pacman::p_load(
    tidyverse, ggtext, showtext, scales, glue, 
  janitor, ggview, readxl, magick, janitor
)
})

# Source utility functions
suppressMessages(
  source(here::here("R/utils/fonts.R")))
  source(here::here("R/utils/social_icons.R"))
  source(here::here("R/themes/base_theme.R"))

### |- figure size ----
fig_w <- 10
fig_dpi <- 320
fig_h <- 6.22

### |-  fonts ----
setup_fonts()
fonts <- get_font_families()
title_family <- fonts$title_1
text_family <- fonts$text
cap_family <- fonts$caption
```

#### [2. Read in the Data]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: read
#| include: true
#| eval: true
#| warning: false

xl_path <- here::here("data/MakeoverMonday/2026/hot_air_balloon.xlsx")

df_raw <- read_excel(
  xl_path,
  skip = 1,
  col_types = "text",
  na = character(),
  .name_repair = "unique"
) |>
  clean_names()
```

#### [3. Examine the Data]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: examine
#| include: true
#| eval: true
#| results: 'hide'
#| warning: false

# split records
df_raw <- df_raw |>
  mutate(
    is_record = str_detect(balloon_id, "^HAB-\\d{6}$"),
    record_no = cumsum(is_record)
  )

glimpse(df_raw)
```

#### [4. Tidy Data]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: tidy
#| warning: false

### |- reattach the split records ----
fragments <- df_raw |>
  filter(!is_record) |>
  summarise(
    owners_cont = paste(balloon_id, collapse = " "),
    across(c(name, registration, manufacturer, model, serial_number, year_built, size), last),
    .by = record_no
  ) |>
  mutate(
    record_no, owners_cont,
    image_f = name, seen_f = registration, crewed_f = manufacturer,
    flown_f = model, burner_time_f = serial_number,
    additional_images_f = year_built, notes_f = size,
    .keep = "none"
  )

balloons <- df_raw |>
  filter(is_record) |>
  left_join(fragments, by = "record_no") |>
  mutate(
    previous_owners = if_else(is.na(owners_cont), previous_owners,
      str_squish(paste(previous_owners, owners_cont))
    ),
    image = coalesce(image_f, image),
    seen = coalesce(seen_f, seen),
    crewed = coalesce(crewed_f, crewed),
    flown = coalesce(flown_f, flown),
    burner_time = coalesce(burner_time_f, burner_time),
    additional_images = coalesce(additional_images_f, additional_images),
    notes = coalesce(notes_f, notes)
  ) |>
  select(balloon_id:notes)

### |- parse fields ----
balloons <- balloons |>
  mutate(
    # first four-digit year = original build; 4 impossible values (2969, 2997 x2,
    # 6077) and 3 malformed ones ("200", "2-14", "2-22") become NA
    build_year = suppressWarnings(as.integer(str_extract(year_built, "^\\d{4}"))),
    build_year = if_else(build_year > 2026, NA_integer_, build_year),
    volume_cuft = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(
      str_remove_all(str_extract(size, "^[\\d,]+(?=\\s*cu)"), ",")
    )),
    in_us_state = location %in% c(state.name, "District of Columbia")
  )

### |- giant threshold: FAI size class AX-11 and above ----
# FAI Sporting Code Section 1 (Aug 2026), 2.1.2: category 11 = 6,000-9,000 m3
cuft_per_m3 <- 35.3147
giant_m3 <- 6000
giant_cuft <- giant_m3 * cuft_per_m3

### |- the three build periods compared ----
periods <- tibble(
  period = c("2000–2009", "2010–2019", "2020–2026"),
  from   = c(2000L, 2010L, 2020L),
  to     = c(2009L, 2019L, 2026L)
)

sized <- balloons |>
  filter(!is.na(volume_cuft), !is.na(build_year)) |>
  inner_join(periods, by = join_by(between(build_year, from, to))) |>
  mutate(giant = volume_cuft > giant_cuft)

us_summary <- sized |>
  filter(in_us_state) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(), k = sum(giant), median_cuft = median(volume_cuft),
    .by = period
  ) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  mutate(
    pct   = 100 * k / n,
    units = round(pct)
  )

outside_summary <- sized |>
  filter(!in_us_state) |>
  summarise(n = n(), k = sum(giant), .by = period) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * k / n)

typical_cuft <- unique(us_summary$median_cuft)

### |- unit grids: 10 x 10 per period ----
grid_df <- us_summary |>
  select(period, units) |>
  reframe(i = 1:100, .by = c(period, units)) |>
  mutate(
    col  = (i - 1) %% 10,
    row  = 9 - (i - 1) %/% 10,
    kind = factor(if_else(i <= units, "giant", "other"), levels = c("giant", "other"))
  )

grid_labels <- us_summary |>
  mutate(
    label = glue("{sprintf('%.1f', pct)}%  ·  {k} of {comma(n)} recorded builds"),
    x = 4.5, y = -1.25
  )
```

#### [5. Visualization Parameters]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: params
#| include: true
#| warning: false

### |- plot aesthetics ----
colors <- get_theme_colors(
  palette = list(
    paper  = "#f4f1ea",
    ink    = "#2b2b2b",
    muted  = "#6f6a63",
    accent = "#722F37",
    square = "#c9c4ba"
  )
)
clrs <- colors$palette
col_paper <- clrs$paper
col_ink <- clrs$ink
col_muted <- clrs$muted
col_accent <- clrs$accent
col_square <- clrs$square

### |- titles and caption ----
title_text <- "The typical balloon stayed the same size.\nGiants became more common."

subtitle_text <- paste0(
  "Hot-air balloons recorded in US states, by the year they were built.\n",
  glue("The median rated envelope volume was {comma(typical_cuft)} cu ft in every period.")
)

key_labels <- c(
  giant = glue("Giant: rated over {comma(round(giant_cuft, -2))} cu ft, more than twice the typical balloon"),
  other = "All other recorded balloons"
)

note_text <- paste(
  glue("Giant = FAI size class AX-11 or larger (over {comma(giant_m3)} m³)."),
  "Squares rounded to whole percents; balloons without a rated size or build year excluded.",
  glue(
    "Outside US states: ",
    paste(glue("{sprintf('%.1f', outside_summary$pct)}% ({outside_summary$k} of {outside_summary$n})"), collapse = ", "),
    "."
  ),
  "A balloonist's archive, not a census of production; 2026 is partial."
)

caption_text <- paste0(
  note_text, "<br>",
  create_mm_caption(
    mm_year = 2026,
    mm_week = 45,
    source_text = "The Hot Air Balloon Database, via Kaggle"
  )
)

### |- plot theme ----
base_theme <- create_base_theme(colors)

weekly_theme <- extend_weekly_theme(
  base_theme,
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = col_paper, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = col_paper, colour = NA),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      family = text_family, face = "bold", size = rel(1.05),
      colour = col_ink, margin = margin(b = 8)
    ),
    panel.spacing = unit(40, "pt"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(
      family = text_family, size = rel(0.72), colour = col_muted,
      margin = margin(b = 4)
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(family = text_family, size = rel(0.72), colour = col_ink),
    legend.key.size = unit(11, "pt"),
    legend.key.spacing.y = unit(3, "pt"),
    legend.margin = margin(t = 2, b = 6),
    plot.title = element_text(
      family = title_family, size = rel(1.72), colour = col_ink,
      lineheight = 1.05, margin = margin(b = 8)
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      family = text_family, size = rel(0.80), colour = col_muted,
      lineheight = 1.3, margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    plot.caption = element_textbox_simple(
      family = cap_family, size = rel(0.45), colour = col_muted,
      lineheight = 1.3, margin = margin(t = 12)
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(16, 60, 12, 60)
  )
)

theme_set(weekly_theme)
```

#### [6. Plot]{.smallcaps}

```{r}
#| label: plot
#| warning: false

### |-  main plot ----
p <- ggplot(grid_df, aes(x = col, y = row)) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = kind, colour = kind),
    width = 0.84, height = 0.84, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = grid_labels,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    family = text_family, size = 3.2, colour = col_ink
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(giant = col_accent, other = col_square),
    labels = key_labels,
    name = "Each square: 1 in every 100 recorded builds"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(giant = col_paper, other = col_muted),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.6, 9.6), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1.9, 9.6), expand = expansion(0)) +
  facet_wrap(~period) +
  coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, caption = caption_text)
```

#### [10. References]{.smallcaps}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
##### Expand for References

**Primary Data (Makeover Monday):** 1.
Makeover Monday `r current_year` Week `r current_week`: `r create_link("Hot Air Balloons", mm_page)` - Workbook: one sheet, 7,934 rows × 22 fields below a title row.
A line break inside the previous-owners field split 412 records across 699 extra rows; rebuilt, the file holds 7,235 balloons (IDs HAB-000001 to HAB-007235, none missing), matching the archive's own counter, and 55 manufacturers, also matching.
- Build year parses for 6,920 balloons (the first year listed; rebuild dates ignored; seven impossible or malformed values treated as missing).
- Size is the model's rated envelope volume in cubic feet, taken from the catalog, not measured per balloon.

**Source Data:** 2.
The Hot Air Balloon Database.
`r create_link("thehabdatabase.com", source_article)`, via Kaggle (matthuff4): `r create_link("Hot Air Balloon dataset", data_source)`.
A community archive of recorded balloons, not a census of production; snapshot date not stated.

**Original Visualization:** 3.
The Hot Air Balloon Database homepage: three counters ("7,235 balloons documented", "55 manufacturers represented", "6,205 pilots & owners connected").
The first two are reproduced exactly from the file; the third could not be reproduced, because its definition isn't stated, so it is not used.

**Classification:** 4.
FAI (2026).
`r create_link("Sporting Code Section 1 – Aerostats, version 3.0", "https://www.fai.org/sites/default/files/2026-07/SC01%20August%202026%20v3.0.pdf")`, effective 1 August 2026, para 2.1.2: size category 11 = 6,000 to 9,000 m³.
5.
Cameron Balloons.
`r create_link("A-Type envelope specifications", "https://cameronballoons.com/?p=16")`: the A-210 (210,000 cu ft) is AX-10 and the A-225 (225,000 cu ft) is AX-11, consistent with the 6,000 m³ boundary.

**Analysis Frame:** - **Population:** balloons recorded in US states (50 states plus DC) with a rated size and a build year.
- **Periods:** 2000–2009, 2010–2019 and 2020–2026 (2026 is partial).
Earlier decades are thinly recorded in the archive and are not shown.
- **Giant:** rated over 6,000 m³ (211,888 cu ft), FAI class AX-11 or larger; more than twice the median.
Near the line, only three rated volumes occur: 210,000 (AX-10), 211,000 (Raven/Aerostar S-77A, still AX-10) and 225,000 (AX-11).
- **Shares:** 26 of 1,198 (2.2%), 78 of 914 (8.5%) and 67 of 675 (9.9%).
The grids round these to whole percents: 2, 9 and 10 squares.
- **Typical balloon:** median rated volume of 90,000 cu ft in all three periods.
- **Outside US states:** 10 of 210 (4.8%), 11 of 211 (5.2%) and 10 of 186 (5.4%).
- **Scope:** counts describe the archive's records, not the market.
The chart makes no claim about why giants became more common.
:::

#### [11. Custom Functions Documentation]{.smallcaps}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
##### 📦 Custom Helper Functions

This analysis uses custom functions from my personal module library for efficiency and consistency across projects.

**Functions Used:**

- **`fonts.R`**: `setup_fonts()`, `get_font_families()` - Font management with showtext
- **`social_icons.R`**: `create_social_caption()` - Generates formatted social media captions
- **`base_theme.R`**: `create_base_theme()`, `extend_weekly_theme()`, `get_theme_colors()` - Custom ggplot2 themes

**Why custom functions?**\
These utilities standardize theming, fonts, and output across all my data visualizations.
The core analysis (data tidying and visualization logic) uses only standard tidyverse packages.

**Source Code:**\
View all custom functions → [GitHub: R/utils](https://github.com/poncest/personal-website/tree/master/R)
